habitat: Singly or in pairs in woodland, thornveld or bushveld. It catches insects on the ground from a perch.
summary: A common resident. The tail has a small indentation at the tip, not a distinct fork, and the outer tail feathers are straight. The bill is delicate, and the iris is dark brown. The sexes are alike. It utters low sibilant swee or swee-ur. The account does not name the body colour. The Kemp name Black Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

tail.shape: A small indentation at the tip, not a distinct fork. The outer feathers are straight.

viewNotes.note: The tail tip has a small indentation, not a fork.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The account does not name the body colour, so none is stored. The grade A file is a begging call from the North West. The Kemp name Black Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.
